data.output:
{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash --login

# Flux batch script (translated from LSF)

# LSF requested:
#   -nnodes 1
#   -G uiuc
#   -W 720
#   -J mirge_Y0
#   -q pbatch
#   -o runOutput.%J
#   -e runError.%J

flux alloc \
  -N 1 \
  --time=12h \
  --queue=pbatch \
  bash -lc '

# Approximate LSF %J using Flux job id.
exec >"runOutput.${FLUX_JOB_ID}" 2>"runError.${FLUX_JOB_ID}"

# NOTE: LSF -G uiuc (account/group) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none for runtime, but accounting/charging/allocation association may be incorrect
# or job may fail if group selection is required.

# NOTE: LSF job name (-J mirge_Y0) has no universally portable Flux batch directive.
# Performance implication: none (metadata only), but job identification in monitoring/accounting may be less clear.

module load gcc/7.3.1
module load spectrum-mpi

conda deactivate
conda activate mirgeDriver.Y1nozzle

export PYOPENCL_CTX="port:tesla"
#export PYOPENCL_CTX="0:2"

# NOTE: This workflow uses jsrun (IBM Spectrum LSF launcher). Flux does not provide a portable equivalent.
# Performance implication: if jsrun is not available/appropriate under Flux on your system, the job may fail to
# launch or may not use allocated resources efficiently.
jsrun_cmd="jsrun -g 1 -a 1 -n 1"

export XDG_CACHE_HOME="/tmp/$USER/xdg-scratch"

$jsrun_cmd js_task_info
$jsrun_cmd python -u -m mpi4py ./nozzle.py
'
"
}
